parameters.label: Human Enemy Health
parameters.description: Changes how much damage human enemies can take before they die.
parameters.rationale: Changes how much damage human enemies can take before they die.
parameters.interaction: Your Weapon Damage affects the same time-to-kill from the opposite side. Raising enemy health while lowering your weapon damage compounds the effect.

parameters.label: Human Enemy Gun Damage
parameters.description: Changes how much damage you take from firearm hits by human enemies.
parameters.rationale: Changes how much damage you take from firearm hits by human enemies.
parameters.interaction: Human Enemy Health controls how long enemies survive; this controls how dangerous their shots are. Repeated-Hit Protection can also affect how sustained incoming fire feels.

parameters.label: Human Attack Frequency
parameters.description: Controls how frequently human enemies can make another attack.
parameters.rationale: Controls how frequently human enemies can make another attack.
parameters.logic: 100% is vanilla. Above 100% shortens the underlying attack cooldown and makes attacks more frequent; below 100% lengthens the cooldown and gives you more breathing room. This does not change weapon fire rate or burst length.
parameters.interaction: Combine this with Human Enemy Gun Damage and Human Enemy Fire Accuracy to shape how relentless human firefights feel.

parameters.label: Human Enemy Fire Accuracy
parameters.description: Changes how accurate human enemy gunfire is.
parameters.rationale: Changes how accurate human enemy gunfire is.
parameters.interaction: Pair it with Human Enemy Gun Damage to tune how threatening firefights feel. It affects human gunfire, not mutant attacks, melee, or grenades.

parameters.label: Explosion Damage
parameters.description: Changes damage from explosions such as grenades and other explosive effects.
parameters.rationale: Changes damage from explosions such as grenades and other explosive effects.
parameters.interaction: Each explosion still has its own base damage. This setting scales the difficulty layer applied on top of those base values.

parameters.label: Your Weapon Damage
parameters.description: Changes the base damage dealt by your weapons.
parameters.rationale: Changes the base damage dealt by your weapons.
parameters.interaction: Your Headshot Damage adds another layer on headshots. Human Enemy Health also changes the final time-to-kill.

parameters.label: Your Headshot Damage
parameters.description: Scales the damage multiplier applied to your headshots; 1x is normal and 2x doubles the configured headshot damage.
parameters.rationale: Controls your headshot damage multiplier, not a separate bonus added to the hit.
parameters.logic: 1.0x is the normal multiplier. 2.0x doubles the headshot damage multiplier used by the selected Base Preset; it is not an additive extra-damage percentage.
parameters.interaction: Your Weapon Damage also affects the underlying hit. The headshot multiplier scales that hit; changing both settings compounds their effect.

parameters.label: Weapon Jamming Frequency
parameters.description: Changes how often worn weapons jam.
parameters.rationale: Changes how often worn weapons jam.
parameters.interaction: Weapon condition and each weapon's own jam behavior still matter. Use this to make jams generally more or less common.

parameters.label: Mutant Hit Damage
parameters.description: Changes how much damage mutant attacks deal when they connect.
parameters.rationale: Changes how much damage mutant attacks deal when they connect.
parameters.interaction: Mutant Health controls how much damage they can absorb; this control changes only damage dealt to the player.

parameters.label: Repeated-Hit Protection - Maximum
parameters.description: Sets the stronger end of the hidden protection the game can apply when several hits land close together.
parameters.rationale: Sets the stronger end of the hidden protection the game can apply when several hits land close together.
parameters.logic: Higher values mean stronger repeated-hit protection and generally easier sustained incoming fire. Lower values reduce that protection. This number is a strength setting, not a literal damage-reduction percentage.
parameters.interaction: Use it together with Repeated-Hit Protection - Minimum. Human Enemy Gun Damage still controls the damage of each individual bullet hit.

parameters.label: Repeated-Hit Protection - Minimum
parameters.description: Sets the weaker end of the hidden protection the game can apply when several hits land close together.
parameters.rationale: Sets the weaker end of the hidden protection the game can apply when several hits land close together.
parameters.logic: Higher values mean more protection at the weak end of the system; lower values make repeated hits harsher. This number is a strength setting, not a literal damage-reduction percentage.
parameters.interaction: Use it together with Repeated-Hit Protection - Maximum. For a vanilla-like setup, keep Minimum at or below Maximum.

parameters.label: Healed Damage Still Counts
parameters.description: Controls whether damage remains in the repeated-hit protection tracker after you heal it.
parameters.rationale: Repeated-hit protection tracks damage taken over time. When this is ON, healing restores your HP but does not immediately erase that healed damage from the protection tracker, so earlier hits can still contribute to repeated-hit protection. When it is OFF, healed damage no longer remains part of that tracked damage. This does not reduce healing strength or make medkits restore less health.
parameters.logic: OFF matches Novice and Stalker. ON matches Veteran and Master. Healing always restores HP normally; this toggle only decides whether the healed portion is still remembered by the repeated-hit protection system.
parameters.interaction: Works with Repeated-Hit Protection - Minimum and Maximum. Healing can either clear old damage from the protection system or let it continue to count, depending on this switch.

parameters.label: Psy Phantom Spawn-Cycle Delay
parameters.description: Controls how long Psy encounters using the Master override wait before another phantom spawn cycle can begin.

notes: Novice/Stalker/Veteran contain no PsyPhantomNPCOverrides block; the UI represents absence as neutral 1.0 / Off. Creating equivalent overrides in Novice/Stalker/Veteran requires runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Controls how long Psy encounters using the Master override wait before another phantom spawn cycle can begin.
parameters.logic: Lower percentages mean new phantom waves can return sooner. Master uses 50% of the normal wait time; 100% represents no extra Master override.
parameters.interaction: Psy Phantom Count controls how many phantoms are added per cycle. Shorter delays and higher counts compound quickly.

parameters.label: Psy Phantom Count
parameters.description: Controls how many Psy phantoms the Master override adds to the affected encounters.

notes: Novice/Stalker/Veteran contain no PsyPhantomNPCOverrides block; the UI represents absence as neutral 1.0 / Off. Creating equivalent overrides in Novice/Stalker/Veteran requires runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Controls how many Psy phantoms the Master override adds to the affected encounters.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps the normal count. 200% matches vanilla Master and doubles the configured phantom count.
parameters.interaction: Spawn-Cycle Delay changes how quickly another wave can happen; this setting changes the size of each wave.

parameters.label: Psy Phantoms Cause Bleeding
parameters.description: Lets the affected Master Psy phantoms inflict bleeding in addition to their normal threat.

notes: Novice/Stalker/Veteran contain no PsyPhantomNPCOverrides block; the UI represents absence as neutral 1.0 / Off. Creating equivalent overrides in Novice/Stalker/Veteran requires runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Lets the affected Master Psy phantoms inflict bleeding in addition to their normal threat.
parameters.logic: OFF keeps this extra bleeding rule disabled. ON matches the Master override.
parameters.interaction: Bleeding Effect Strength and bleeding treatment still control how dangerous and recoverable the resulting bleeding is.

parameters.label: Psy Equipment Durability Damage
parameters.description: Controls how much equipment durability the affected Master Psy enemies damage.

notes: Novice/Stalker/Veteran contain no PsyPhantomNPCOverrides block; the UI represents absence as neutral 1.0 / Off. Creating equivalent overrides in Novice/Stalker/Veteran requires runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Controls how much equipment durability the affected Master Psy enemies damage.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps normal durability damage. 200% matches vanilla Master and doubles this durability damage.
parameters.interaction: This does not change their direct health damage. Armor/helmet durability settings still affect how your gear wears overall.

parameters.label: Energy Drink Fatigue Relief
parameters.description: Scales the amount of accumulated fatigue removed by energy-drink sleepiness-reduction effects.

notes: Runtime EffectPrototypes.cfg exposes direct energy-drink SleepinessPoints relief (-20), the Weird Kettle limited-energy alternative (-100), and Poppy Field energy-drink regeneration effects (-3.5 and -5.0).
The slider scales only those energy-drink fatigue-relief values; passive player RegenSleepinessPoints remains controlled separately by Fatigue Build-up Rate.

parameters.rationale: Lets the player tune how strongly energy drinks counter fatigue without changing how quickly fatigue naturally accumulates.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps vanilla fatigue relief. 50% halves it, 200% doubles it, and 0% makes energy drinks provide no fatigue relief.
parameters.interaction: Fatigue Build-up Rate controls how quickly tiredness returns. This setting changes how much relief energy drinks provide, including their special Poppy Field and Weird Kettle variants.

parameters.interaction: Instant Stamina Restore and Energy Drink Fatigue Relief remain separate controls.

The separate OverDrunknessMechanics chain is not silently folded into this scalar.
The obsolete VeryStrongDrunkness target was removed because that node is not present in the audited current CFG.

parameters.rationale: Retained as a source-correct internal mapping while OverDrunkness remains separately audited.
parameters.logic: At 1x, Medium = 30 and Strong = 80. Low remains at its authored near-zero boundary.
parameters.interaction: Not player-facing yet; Beer and Vodka direct strength remain the editable alcohol axes.

parameters.label: Beer Strength
parameters.description: Sets Beer drink strength against the current DrunknessMechanics stages: Low 0.001, Medium 30 and Strong 80.

notes: BeerDrunkness uses ValueMin = 15 and ValueMax = 15 in the audited vanilla-era/current mod cross-check.
The control writes the same raw Drunkness value to ValueMin and ValueMax in exact 1-point steps.
The direct effect fields are source-structured and writer-safe, but the exact 2.0.5 raw row was not part of the original project baseline and should be runtime-tested.

parameters.rationale: Controls how strongly one Beer pushes the drunkenness meter.
parameters.logic: Vanilla is 15 Drunkness per Beer. Against the current Medium 30 / Strong 80 stage boundaries, back-to-back vanilla Beer reaches Medium on the 2nd drink and Strong on the 6th.
parameters.interaction: Always visible beside Vodka Strength. Moving it updates Beer strength, the Beer Strong-stage drink count, and the back-to-back progression immediately.

parameters.label: Vodka Strength
parameters.description: Sets how much Drunkness one Vodka adds against the current DrunknessMechanics stage boundaries.

notes: VodkaDrunkness uses ValueMin = 30 and ValueMax = 30 in the audited vanilla-era/current mod cross-check.
The control writes the same raw Drunkness value to ValueMin and ValueMax in exact 5-point steps.
The direct effect fields are source-structured and writer-safe, but the exact 2.0.5 raw row was not part of the original project baseline and should be runtime-tested.

parameters.rationale: Controls how strongly one Vodka pushes the drunkenness meter.

parameters.interaction: Always visible beside Beer Strength. Moving it updates Vodka strength, the Vodka Strong-stage drink count, and the back-to-back progression immediately.

parameters.label: Sleep Becomes Available At
parameters.description: Controls how tired the player must be before normal sleeping is allowed.
parameters.rationale: Controls how tired the player must be before normal sleeping is allowed.
parameters.logic: Higher values require more accumulated sleepiness before sleep becomes available; lower values allow sleeping earlier.
parameters.interaction: Separate no-sleep effects from hunger, bleeding, radiation or Psy can still block sleep regardless of this threshold.

parameters.label: Minimum Sleep
parameters.description: Sets the minimum sleep duration used by the default sleep settings.
parameters.rationale: Sets the minimum sleep duration used by the default sleep settings.
parameters.interaction: This is a time requirement, not a direct setting for how much each restorative effect heals.

parameters.label: Radiation Accumulation
parameters.description: Scales the rate at which radiation is accumulated through the difficulty preset.
parameters.rationale: Scales the rate at which radiation is accumulated through the difficulty preset.
parameters.interaction: Radiation Recovery controls passive reduction separately. Master Radiation Mechanics can also add a stamina penalty at high radiation.

parameters.label: Radiation Recovery
parameters.description: Controls how quickly accumulated radiation decreases naturally, in points per second.
parameters.rationale: Controls how quickly accumulated radiation decreases naturally, in points per second.
parameters.interaction: This acts on recovery, not exposure strength. Radiation Accumulation determines how quickly new radiation is gained.

parameters.label: Radiation Damage
parameters.description: Changes how much health damage accumulated radiation causes once radiation begins hurting you, without moving the vanilla radiation-state thresholds.

notes: Aggregate transform over the 11 runtime radiation-damage effect prototypes; radiation thresholds remain vanilla.
The runtime values are not replaced by one universal damage number; each stage keeps its original relative value.

parameters.rationale: Controls the health damage caused by radiation after the game has already decided that your current radiation level should hurt you.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps vanilla radiation damage. 50% halves it, 200% doubles it, 600% multiplies it by six, and 1000% multiplies it by ten. Original stage thresholds stay vanilla.
parameters.interaction: Radiation Accumulation controls how quickly radiation builds up. Radiation Recovery and Anti-Rad control how quickly it is removed. The Master radiation bundle adds a separate stamina penalty.

parameters.label: Bleeding Severity
parameters.description: Scales the difficulty-wide bleeding effect applied by sources that cause bleeding.
parameters.rationale: Scales the difficulty-wide bleeding effect applied by sources that cause bleeding.
parameters.logic: Higher values make bleeding effects stronger overall; lower values soften them. Novice uses 25%, Stalker/Veteran 100%, and Master 150%.
parameters.interaction: Low / Medium / Severe Bleeding Damage decide how much HP you lose once each bleeding state is active. Natural Bleeding Recovery and medical treatment decide how quickly bleeding goes away.

parameters.label: Natural Bleeding Recovery
parameters.description: Controls the player's base natural bleeding reduction rate.
parameters.rationale: Controls the player's base natural bleeding reduction rate.
parameters.interaction: Bandages and medkits apply direct bleeding removal independently of this passive rate.

parameters.label: Player Max Health
parameters.description: Changes your maximum health. The game's full-health feedback stays in sync with the new maximum.

notes: Direct MaxHP field is confirmed; broader assumptions about the 100-point HP scale require runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Changes your maximum health. The game's full-health feedback stays in sync with the new maximum.
parameters.interaction: The game keeps its vanilla low-health state boundary. Other systems may also assume a 100-point health scale, so very large Max Health changes should be tested in game.

parameters.label: Passive Health Recovery
parameters.description: Controls ordinary passive health recovery on the player. Vanilla sets this to zero, so by default you do not slowly heal just by standing around.

notes: Field and vanilla value are confirmed; exact tick semantics and interaction with effect-based regeneration require runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Controls ordinary passive health recovery on the player. Vanilla sets this to zero, so by default you do not slowly heal just by standing around.
parameters.logic: Zero keeps vanilla behavior. Raising it adds passive healing over time.
parameters.interaction: Health Recovery Delay decides when recovery can begin. Other healing sources, such as low-health recovery and medkits, stay separate.

parameters.label: Health Recovery Delay
parameters.description: Vanilla player VitalParams define RegenHPDelayTimeSeconds = 5.

notes: The field explicitly uses seconds; the exact set of regeneration sources that honor it requires runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Sets how many seconds must pass before health recovery can begin. Vanilla is 5 seconds.
parameters.logic: Higher values postpone actor-level HP regeneration for longer; lower values shorten the configured delay.
parameters.interaction: If Passive Health Recovery is set to 0, this delay may have no visible effect until another compatible health-recovery effect is active.

parameters.label: Health Recovery Multiplier
parameters.description: Scales health regeneration produced by compatible recovery effects. It does not create passive healing by itself: 100% keeps full effect strength, while lower values weaken that recovery.
parameters.rationale: Changes the strength of health-recovery effects that are already active. It does not create passive healing by itself.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps compatible regeneration effects at full strength. Lower values weaken them; higher values strengthen them. Vanilla uses 100% on Novice/Stalker, 75% on Veteran and 50% on Master.
parameters.interaction: Passive Health Recovery is 0 in vanilla, so this matters mainly when another effect is already restoring health, such as low-health recovery.

parameters.label: Low-Health Recovery Rate
parameters.description: Controls the positive health-regeneration rate supplied by the normal low-health recovery effect. Vanilla uses 1.0; higher values recover health faster while the effect is active, and 0 disables this recovery contribution.
parameters.rationale: Sets the recovery speed used by the normal low-health recovery effect. Vanilla is 1 HP/s.
parameters.interaction: Health Recovery Multiplier can scale this effect, and the Master low-health penalty can reduce it further.

parameters.label: Master Low-Health Mechanics
parameters.description: Turns on the extra low-health punishment used by vanilla Master.
parameters.rationale: Turns on the extra low-health punishment used by vanilla Master.
parameters.logic: OFF leaves only the normal low-health system. ON adds the extra Master recovery penalty whenever the game enters its Master low-health state.
parameters.interaction: The game keeps the vanilla activation point for this state. The child control only changes how strong the recovery penalty is.

parameters.label: Master Low-Health Recovery Penalty
parameters.description: Controls how strongly Master difficulty slows health recovery when you are badly wounded.
parameters.rationale: Controls how strongly Master difficulty slows health recovery when you are badly wounded.
parameters.logic: Higher values suppress health regeneration more strongly; zero removes this penalty component.
parameters.interaction: This remains inactive while Master Low-Health Mechanics is OFF. It layers on top of ordinary low-health recovery and the Health Recovery Multiplier setting.

parameters.label: Healing Amount
parameters.description: Changes how much HP the main healing items restore.
parameters.rationale: Set HP restored by Bandages, Medkits, Army Medkits, and Scientific Medkits. Bleeding and radiation removal are controlled separately.

parameters.label: Medkit Healing
parameters.description: Controls how much health a standard Medkit restores before any Master-only healing penalty is applied.
parameters.rationale: Controls how much health a standard Medkit restores before any Master-only healing penalty is applied.
parameters.interaction: Bleeding treatment is separate. If Master Consumable Effect Penalties are ON, the Master Medkit Healing setting further changes the final heal.

parameters.label: Army Medkit Healing
parameters.description: Controls how much health an Army Medkit restores before any Master-only healing penalty is applied.
parameters.rationale: Controls how much health an Army Medkit restores before any Master-only healing penalty is applied.
parameters.interaction: Bleeding treatment is separate. If Master Consumable Effect Penalties are ON, Master Army Medkit Healing further changes the final heal.

parameters.label: Scientific Medkit Healing
parameters.description: Controls how much health a Scientific Medkit restores. Vanilla restores 100 HP.
parameters.rationale: Controls how much health a Scientific Medkit restores. Vanilla restores 100 HP.
parameters.interaction: Scientific Medkit bleeding and radiation treatment are separate. Vanilla Master does not apply the same healing penalty to Scientific Medkits that it applies to Bandages and the other Medkits.

parameters.label: Food Restores Health
parameters.description: Controls whether ordinary food restores health. This affects Bread, Fresh Bread, Canned Food, and Sausage only. Satiety and Weird Kettle alternative effects are intentionally unchanged.
parameters.rationale: Separates food from medical healing. OFF removes the normal HP restoration from the four ordinary healing-food effects while preserving hunger/satiety and every Weird Kettle alternative effect.
parameters.logic: ON keeps vanilla food healing. OFF removes healing from the supported food items.
parameters.interaction: Bandage healing remains controlled by the Healing Amount radar. Weird Kettle alternative food effects are deliberately outside this switch.

parameters.label: Master Bandage Healing
parameters.description: Controls how much of the normal Bandage healing remains while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are active. Vanilla Master keeps 25% of the normal heal.
parameters.rationale: Controls how much of the normal Bandage healing remains while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are active. Vanilla Master keeps 25% of the normal heal.
parameters.logic: 100% means no Master healing penalty. Lower values make the Bandage heal less. With the untouched base heal of 20 HP, vanilla Master gives about 5.0 HP.
parameters.interaction: This setting only has an effect while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are ON. Changing both the base heal and this Master percentage compounds the result.

parameters.label: Master Medkit Healing
parameters.description: Controls how much of the normal Medkit healing remains while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are active. Vanilla Master keeps 71% of the normal heal.
parameters.rationale: Controls how much of the normal Medkit healing remains while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are active. Vanilla Master keeps 71% of the normal heal.
parameters.logic: 100% means no Master healing penalty. Lower values make the Medkit heal less. With the untouched base heal of 70 HP, vanilla Master gives about 49.7 HP.
parameters.interaction: This setting only has an effect while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are ON. Changing both the base heal and this Master percentage compounds the result.

parameters.label: Master Army Medkit Healing
parameters.description: Controls how much of the normal Army Medkit healing remains while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are active. Vanilla Master keeps 82% of the normal heal.
parameters.rationale: Controls how much of the normal Army Medkit healing remains while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are active. Vanilla Master keeps 82% of the normal heal.
parameters.logic: 100% means no Master healing penalty. Lower values make the Army Medkit heal less. With the untouched base heal of 85 HP, vanilla Master gives about 69.7 HP.
parameters.interaction: This setting only has an effect while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are ON. Changing both the base heal and this Master percentage compounds the result.

parameters.label: Bandage Bleeding Removal
parameters.description: Controls how much bleeding the Bandage removes when used.
parameters.rationale: Controls how much bleeding the Bandage removes when used.
parameters.interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Natural Bleeding Recovery and bleeding damage remain separate.

parameters.label: Medkit Bleeding Removal
parameters.description: Controls how much bleeding the Medkit removes when used.
parameters.rationale: Controls how much bleeding the Medkit removes when used.
parameters.interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Natural Bleeding Recovery and bleeding damage remain separate.

parameters.description: Controls how much bleeding the Army Medkit removes when used.
parameters.rationale: Controls how much bleeding the Army Medkit removes when used.
parameters.interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Natural Bleeding Recovery and bleeding damage remain separate.

parameters.description: Controls how much bleeding the Scientific Medkit removes when used.
parameters.rationale: Controls how much bleeding the Scientific Medkit removes when used.
parameters.interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Natural Bleeding Recovery and bleeding damage remain separate.

parameters.label: Scientific Medkit Radiation Removal
parameters.description: Controls how much radiation the Scientific Medkit removes when used.
parameters.rationale: Controls how much radiation the Scientific Medkit removes when used.
parameters.interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Radiation build-up and natural radiation recovery remain separate.

parameters.description: Controls how much radiation the Anti-Rad removes when used.
parameters.rationale: Controls how much radiation the Anti-Rad removes when used.
parameters.interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Radiation build-up and natural radiation recovery remain separate.

parameters.label: Maximum Stamina
parameters.description: Vanilla maximum stamina is 100. This changes the size of your stamina pool, not how fast it recovers or how much actions cost.
parameters.rationale: Changes your maximum stamina pool. Vanilla is 100.
parameters.interaction: Action costs are direct stamina values, so changing Maximum Stamina changes how many actions fit into a full bar even when their individual costs are untouched.

notes: Runtime 2.0.5 Player.VitalParams.MaxSP = 100.

parameters.label: Sprint Stops Below
parameters.description: Below this stamina value, sprinting is disabled. Default: 16.1 of the vanilla 100 stamina pool.
parameters.rationale: Sets how low your stamina can fall before sprinting is forced to stop. Vanilla is 16.1 stamina.
parameters.logic: Higher values make sprint lock out earlier while stamina is still relatively high; lower values let the player sprint deeper into the stamina bar.
parameters.interaction: Pairs with Exhaustion Regen Delay; sets sprint lockout, not sprint speed or stamina drain.

notes: The mapped threshold is the entry whose StateTags contains EStateTag::Sprint.

parameters.label: Exhaustion Regen Delay
parameters.description: Seconds before stamina regeneration resumes after sprint exhaustion.
parameters.rationale: Changes how long you must wait after running out of sprint stamina before recovery can begin.
parameters.logic: Higher values make exhaustion pauses last longer before recovery can resume; lower values shorten the pause.
parameters.interaction: Applies after sprint exhaustion; Sprint Stops Below determines the separate lockout threshold.

parameters.label: Boost Starts Below
parameters.description: Below this stamina value, the separate low-stamina recovery boost becomes eligible. Default: 30 stamina.
parameters.rationale: Sets the stamina level that triggers emergency low-stamina recovery. Vanilla is 30 stamina.
parameters.logic: Higher values allow the low-stamina recovery helper to engage across a larger portion of the bar; lower values reserve it for near-exhaustion.
parameters.interaction: Pairs with low-stamina Boost Rate and low-stamina Boost Duration, not the sprint lockout threshold.

notes: The NormalSP boundary is 30; the LowSPThreshold branch starts at 0 and applies IncreaseStaminaPoints below that boundary.

parameters.label: Boost Strength
parameters.description: Regeneration strength of the temporary low-stamina recovery boost (10 stamina/s originally).
parameters.rationale: Sets how strong emergency stamina recovery is while it is active. Vanilla is 10 stamina/s.
parameters.logic: Higher values make the emergency recovery effect stronger; lower values make low-stamina recovery closer to the ordinary base rate.
parameters.interaction: Boost Starts Below sets its trigger; low-stamina Boost Duration sets how long it lasts.

parameters.label: Boost Duration
parameters.description: Seconds that the conditional low-stamina stamina regeneration boost remains active (4 seconds originally).
parameters.rationale: Sets how long emergency stamina recovery lasts once it is triggered. Vanilla is 4 seconds.
parameters.logic: Higher values keep the low-stamina recovery effect active longer; lower values shorten the boost.
parameters.interaction: Boost Activates Below sets the trigger; low-stamina Boost Rate sets the boost strength.

parameters.label: Speed-Limited Sprint Stamina Effect
parameters.description: Changes stamina recovery while you are sprinting but your movement speed is being limited. The game decides when this slower sprint state is active.
parameters.rationale: Changes stamina recovery during speed-limited sprinting.
parameters.logic: More negative values suppress recovery more strongly; zero adds no state penalty; positive values help recovery. Do not read this as a separate 'slow sprint' button.
parameters.interaction: This works alongside normal Sprint stamina behavior. Encumbrance and other movement limits can affect when the game uses this slower sprint state.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in speed-limited sprint state

notes: CFG target is confirmed; exact runtime transition into EStateTag::SprintUnderRunSpeed is not fully documented.

parameters.label: Jogging-State Stamina Effect
parameters.description: Changes stamina recovery during the game's lighter running movement state. There is no separate Jogging keybind.
parameters.rationale: Changes stamina recovery while the game treats your movement as jogging.
parameters.logic: Negative settings slow stamina recovery while jogging; 0 is neutral; positive settings help stamina recover.
parameters.interaction: The game decides when your movement counts as jogging. This setting only affects stamina recovery during that movement.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in internal Jogging state

notes: CFG target EStateTag::Jogging is confirmed; there is no separate player Jogging bind and exact activation semantics require runtime verification.

parameters.label: Slow-Run-State Stamina Effect
parameters.description: Changes stamina recovery during the game's slow-running movement state. There is no separate Slow Run keybind.
parameters.rationale: Changes stamina recovery while the game treats your movement as slow running.
parameters.logic: Negative values add a stamina penalty in the SlowRun state; zero is neutral; positive values help recovery. Do not treat this as the game's Walk toggle.
parameters.interaction: This is separate from walking. The game decides when movement counts as slow running.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in internal SlowRun state

notes: CFG target EStateTag::SlowRun is confirmed; SlowRunThreshold = 0.5 exists, but its complete state-selection semantics are not proven.

parameters.label: Maximum Vault Height
parameters.description: Changes the tallest obstacle you can vault over. The WAIST / EYES / ABOVE EYES markers are simple player-friendly height references.
parameters.rationale: Changes the tallest obstacle you can vault over. The WAIST / EYES / ABOVE EYES markers are simple player-friendly height references.
parameters.logic: Higher values let the vault search accept taller obstacles; lower values restrict vaulting to lower obstacles. The slider is capped at 300 to keep the requested range around vanilla through slightly-above-eye/head traversal rather than turning this into extreme parkour.
parameters.interaction: Vault Stamina Cost still controls the stamina cost of a successful vault. MinObstacleHeight, landing checks, search radius and other vault geometry remain vanilla.

notes: The CFG field and vanilla value are confirmed from runtime 2.0.5.
WAIST/EYES/ABOVE EYES are practical UI orientation points; exact reachable world geometry depends on the rest of VaultingParams and collision/animation constraints.

parameters.label: Medium-Water Stamina Drain
parameters.description: Changes the extra stamina drain while moving through medium-depth water.
parameters.rationale: Changes the extra stamina drain while moving through medium-depth water.
parameters.logic: Higher percentages make movement actions consume more stamina while moderately immersed; lower values soften the water penalty.
parameters.interaction: This changes penalty strength only. Water immersion thresholds remain unchanged.

notes: AffectedStaminaActionTypes: Walk, Run, Sprint, Jump, Vault.

parameters.label: Deep-Water Stamina Drain
parameters.description: Changes the extra stamina drain while moving through deep water.
parameters.rationale: Changes the extra stamina drain while moving through deep water.
parameters.logic: Higher percentages make deep-water movement substantially more expensive; lower values reduce that stamina pressure.
parameters.interaction: This does not change the water-depth thresholds or the separate deadly-water instant-death effect.

notes: AffectedStaminaActionTypes: Walk, Run, Sprint, Jump, Vault.
Deadly water still has a separate WaterDeadlyDamage instant-death effect.

parameters.label: Base Stamina Recovery
parameters.description: Controls the player's base stamina regeneration rate.
parameters.rationale: Controls the player's base stamina regeneration rate.
parameters.interaction: Movement-state values, hunger penalties and fatigue effects can reduce this base regeneration in context.

parameters.label: Action Costs
parameters.description: Changes stamina pressure from common player actions.
parameters.rationale: Set how tiring sprinting, jumping, vaulting, and melee attacks are. The Aiming point changes stamina recovery while aiming rather than charging a one-time action cost.

parameters.label: Jump Stamina Cost
parameters.description: Controls stamina consumed by a jump.
parameters.rationale: Controls stamina consumed by a jump.
parameters.interaction: This is a per-action cost and does not change stamina regeneration.

parameters.label: Vault Stamina Cost
parameters.description: Controls stamina consumed by vaulting.
parameters.rationale: Controls stamina consumed by vaulting.
parameters.interaction: The effect is independent of jump cost even though both affect traversal.

parameters.label: Quick Melee Cost
parameters.description: Controls stamina consumed by a quick melee attack.
parameters.rationale: Controls stamina consumed by a quick melee attack.
parameters.interaction: Strong melee and buttstock attacks have independent costs.

parameters.label: Strong Melee Cost
parameters.description: Controls stamina consumed by a strong melee attack.
parameters.rationale: Controls stamina consumed by a strong melee attack.
parameters.interaction: This does not alter melee damage, only the stamina economy of the action.

parameters.label: Buttstock Melee Cost
parameters.description: Controls stamina consumed by a buttstock melee attack.
parameters.rationale: Controls stamina consumed by a buttstock melee attack.
parameters.interaction: Normal and strong melee use their own stamina values.

parameters.label: Full Sprint Stamina Effect
parameters.description: Changes stamina recovery while sprinting.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in full sprint state

notes: Player-facing Sprint action; CFG target EStateTag::Sprint is confirmed.

parameters.rationale: Changes stamina recovery while sprinting.
parameters.logic: Lower recovery makes sustained sprinting more exhausting. 0 adds no sprint-specific recovery change; higher recovery lets stamina come back faster.
parameters.interaction: Stacks with Base Stamina Regeneration and the separate Sprint Stamina Drain. Speed-limited sprinting can use the separate SprintUnderRunSpeed state instead.

parameters.label: Run-State Stamina Effect
parameters.description: Changes stamina recovery while the game treats your movement as running.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in internal Run state

notes: CFG target EStateTag::Run is confirmed; exact state-selection semantics versus Jogging/SlowRun require runtime verification.

parameters.rationale: Changes stamina recovery during normal running.
parameters.logic: Negative settings slow stamina recovery while running; 0 is neutral; positive settings help stamina recover.
parameters.interaction: The game switches between several movement states depending on how you move. This setting affects only normal running.

parameters.label: Aiming Regen Penalty
parameters.description: Percent reduction in stamina regeneration specifically while aiming; 0% removes the penalty.

notes: Player-facing Aim state; CFG target EStateTag::Aim is confirmed.
UI stores a positive penalty magnitude; production writer emits the corresponding negative CFG coefficient via negateSet.

parameters.rationale: Controls the aiming-only regeneration penalty independently from low-stamina recovery effects.
parameters.logic: Higher settings slow stamina recovery more while aiming. 0 removes the aiming recovery penalty.
parameters.interaction: This is a continuous recovery-state penalty, not a one-time stamina charge. Base Stamina Recovery sets the underlying recovery rate; Sprint, Jump, Vault and melee costs remain independent.

parameters.label: Maximum Carry Weight
parameters.description: Sets the player's default maximum inventory mass.
parameters.rationale: Sets the player's default maximum inventory mass.
parameters.interaction: Encumbrance thresholds and equipment-derived carry-weight bonuses can affect how the load feels before the absolute maximum is reached.

parameters.label: Extra NPC Corpse Loot
parameters.description: Chooses the extra smart-loot package added to human NPC corpses: Medicine + Ammo, Water, or None.
parameters.rationale: Chooses which extra smart-loot package is added to human NPC corpses on top of their normal generated inventory.
parameters.logic: Choose what extra loot ordinary human corpses can carry: Medicine + Ammo, Water, or None. Enemy progression still affects which items can appear.
parameters.interaction: This sits on top of normal NPC inventory generation. The other NPC loot controls change normal drops and do not replace this extra corpse-loot package.

parameters.label: NPC Medical Drop
parameters.description: Changes how often ordinary human enemies carry Bandages, Medkits, Army Medkits, or Anti-Rad. It does not change how many items are in each stack.

targets.path: medical PossibleItems[*].Chance via standard-human-only redirect manifest

notes: The audited control surface contains 58 medical Chance rows across six shared role-oriented consumable pools.
100% preserves every vanilla Chance; 0% disables those medical rolls; values above 100% multiply each source Chance and clamp at 100%.
Seven source medical rows are already Chance = 1.0 and therefore remain capped at 100% when increasing frequency.
Only 37 audited standard-human SubItemGenerator links are redirected to TCD-owned pool clones; Prologue, zombie, named/scripted and other shared consumers remain vanilla.

parameters.rationale: Changes medical-item drop frequency on ordinary human enemies without changing food, drinks, stimulants, alcohol, or stack sizes.
parameters.logic: 0-200% changes the vanilla medical drop chance. 50% halves it, 100% keeps vanilla, and 200% doubles it up to a maximum of 100%.
parameters.interaction: Affects ordinary human enemies only. It does not change zombies, named/story characters, traders, stash loot, or the amount inside each medical stack.

parameters.label: NPC Ammo Drops
parameters.description: Scales the generic NPC_Ammo_Smart bonus ammunition stacks on ordinary NPC corpses. This is not NPC weapon-attached ammo and not Breakable Box Ammo.

notes: Exact source data: 43 NPC_Ammo_Smart item rows across 24 PrimaryWeaponParams groups and four ranks; matches GameData/StashPrototypes.cfg supplied dump row-for-row (FNV32 0x61073f67).

Only MinCount/MaxCount are scaled in a source-derived clone with integer-half-up rounding; native MinSpawnChance, MaxSpawnChance, PriorityCaliber, MainWeaponAmmoCount, Weight and item/rank eligibility remain inherited.
Only the selected difficulty GeneralNPC CorpseSmartLoot list references the clone. Medicine + Ammo activates it; Water or None leaves the player-selected multiplier saved but causes no ammo override.
Breakable ammo uses the separate ItemGeneratorPrototypes.cfg DestructibleStash_AmmoSNG/NATO generator clones and is never affected by this control.
Legacy weapon-attached AmmoMinCount/AmmoMaxCount edits on 121 NPC weapon rows are retired (242 direct edit points removed).
Actual in-game corpse drop result and source-derived clone inheritance require a Wine build and runtime test.

parameters.rationale: Controls generic bonus ammo counts on ordinary human NPC corpses when the Extra Corpse Loot choice enables Medicine + Ammo. No effect on weapon-attached spare ammo or breakable boxes.
parameters.logic: At 1x, use the source stack amounts from NPC_Ammo_Smart. At 0x, source item counts are zero. Higher settings scale existing counts with integer-half-up, without altering chance or caliber eligibility. Water/None disables the package while retaining this preset value.
parameters.interaction: Extra Corpse Loot activates the bonus package, while the NPC Ammo slider adjusts its item counts. Newbie rank source examples: 12 Gauge 2–6, 5.45 15–20, .45 ACP 8–12. These examples are independent of the Breakable Box Ammo Yield slider.

parameters.label: NPC Weapon Condition
parameters.description: Sets the actual minimum and maximum condition of weapons carried by ordinary repeatable human NPC loadouts. Vanilla is left untouched until this control is changed.

notes: Production-only audit locks this control to 121 direct weapon rows across 33 repeatable standard-human loadout roots.
120 rows use vanilla 25%-50% durability ranges; one row uses 35%-45%. OFF/default behavior emits no patch, so that authored outlier remains untouched.
Once either bound is changed, the selected MIN and MAX become direct MinDurability/MaxDurability values on all 121 audited weapon rows.
Two Prologue roots and four named MIK/Mykluha roots are excluded.

parameters.rationale: Sets the condition range of weapons dropped by ordinary human enemies.
parameters.logic: Default keeps vanilla condition. After changing it, MIN sets the lowest dropped condition and MAX sets the highest; MIN can never be above MAX.
parameters.interaction: Changes only the condition of weapons dropped by ordinary human enemies. It does not change which weapons they use, their ammo, health, traders, zombies, or story characters.

parameters.label: Ammo Stash Weight
parameters.description: Legacy compatibility-only global ammo Weight multiplier across all eligible stash groups and ranks. 1x keeps native Weight, 0x zeros supported Weight entries, 0.1–1x reduces the source Weight compared with unchanged categories. Native Chance entries are not changed by this knob; native bonus Chance has separate controls where exposed.

display.valueLabel: Relative item Weight — not drop chance

notes: 1x keeps native Weight; independently-authored Chance is untouched.
0x zeros only eligible Weight entries, not Chance-only entries; full exclusion is not guaranteed.
Does not independently increase total stash occurrences or turn absent items into available loot.

parameters.rationale: Adjust relative ammo presence without touching ammo stack size or quest rewards.
parameters.logic: Native Weight is relative within its own generator group. Multiplying all members of a single-category pool may leave its normalized ratios unchanged; independent Chance is never modified by this global control.
